documents.title: Getting started
documents.body:
# Getting started

This workspace application is a CRM for your organization. You use it to keep track of the
customers you work with, plan meetings in a shared calendar, talk to colleagues in internal
chat, and receive in-app notifications about things that concern you.

## What you can do today

- **Customers** — keep a list of the companies and individuals you do business with, their
  contact persons, owners and statuses (Workspace → "Customers").
- **Calendar** — create events, invite colleagues as guests, answer invitations and set
  personal reminders ("Calendar" in the left rail).
- **Chat** — internal conversations with colleagues of your organization ("Chat" in the left
  rail).
- **Notifications** — an in-app inbox behind the bell icon in the header.
- **Your own settings** — profile, email, password, signed-in devices, notification choices
  and appearance ("User settings" in the account menu).
- **Organization settings** — organization name, currency, calendar defaults and customer
  numbering; available to administrators only.

## Signing in

Open the sign-in page and fill in "Email" and "Password", then click "Sign in". The field
"Organization (optional)" is the sign-in identifier of your organization; fill it in only if
your administrator told you to.

There is no self-registration: nobody can create an account for themselves. An account is
created for you by someone in your organization on the Users page, together with an initial
password. If you do not have an account, ask your administrator.

If you forgot your password, click "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page. See "Account and
security" for the full flow.

## Roles

Every person has one of two roles:

- **User** (`USER`) — the regular role.
- **Admin** (`ADMIN`) — can additionally open the "Settings" area and change organization-wide
  settings.

You can see your role on the Dashboard ("Role" card) and in User settings → "Account". Only
someone who manages accounts on the Users page can change a role.

## Your first steps

1. Open **User settings → Profile** and fill in your "Name" and, if it differs from the
   organization default, your "Time zone". Your calendar is drawn in this zone.
2. Look at the **Dashboard** (Workspace → "Dashboard"): it shows who you are signed in as, your
   role, since when you are a member, and your "Upcoming Events". At the top there is a
   "Product tour" card: "Open the guide" opens the Guide, and its links ("Modules & services",
   "Development & delivery", "Architecture", "Key subsystems") jump to that part of it. Close
   the card with its "Hide the product tour" button; the Guide stays available in the left
   rail.
3. Open **Customers** to see the organization's customer list.
4. Open **Calendar** to see your week.

## Things that do not exist

To avoid searching for them: there are no tickets, no billing or invoices, no import or export
of data, no bulk actions, no recurring calendar events, no email notifications (notifications
are in-app only), no two-factor authentication, and no mobile app. The interface is available
in English only.

documents.title: Navigation and layout
documents.body:
# Navigation and layout

The screen is split into columns, from left to right.

## 1. The icon rail (far left)

A narrow column of icons, one per **area** of the application. Hover an icon to see its name.
The areas, top to bottom:

| Area | What is inside |
| --- | --- |
| "Workspace" | "Dashboard", "Users", "Customers" |
| "Calendar" | Day, week, month and agenda views of your events |
| "Chat" | Internal conversations with colleagues |
| "Settings" | Organization settings — shown only to administrators |
| "Playground" | A demo of interface components for developers; nothing here affects your data |
| "Guide" | A one-page overview of the product and its modules |

The logo tile at the top takes you to the Workspace. Clicking the icon of the area you are
already in collapses or expands the second column.

## 2. The area sidebar (second column)

Shows the navigation of the active area. At the top you see your organization's name and the
area name. You can drag its right edge to make it wider.

- In **Workspace** it lists "Dashboard", "Users" and "Customers".
- In **Calendar** it shows a small month picker instead of a menu. If your device's time zone
  differs from your calendar time zone, it warns "Times are shown in …" with a link "Change
  your time zone".
- In **Chat** it lists your conversations.
- In **Settings** (administrators) it lists "General", "Calendar", "Numbering", "Activity".
- In **User settings** it lists "Profile", "Account", "Security", "Notifications",
  "Appearance".

At the bottom of the sidebar is your avatar and name. Click it (the "Account menu") to open
"User settings" or to "Log out".

## 3. The header bar

Above the page content, from left to right:

- a button that hides or shows the area sidebar;
- the page title and breadcrumbs (for example "Customers › Acme Inc");
- the **bell** — your notifications. A badge shows how many new notifications arrived since
  you last opened the panel;
- the **theme switcher** ("Switch theme": "Light", "Dark", "System");
- the **assistant button** ("Toggle assistant") — opens this AI assistant; it is present only
  when the assistant is enabled in your installation;
- a **context panel** button ("Show context panel" / "Hide context panel") — appears only when
  the current page has something to show in the context panel.

## 4. The context panel

A column on the right that shows the details of one item next to the page instead of on top
of it. Today it is used for **calendar events**: opening an event in the Calendar, in the
"Upcoming" card of a customer, or in the "Upcoming Events" widget of the Dashboard shows the
event in this panel. It has its own close button and can be resized.

Customers and users open as full pages, not in the context panel.

## 5. The assistant panel

The AI assistant opens as a column at the far right, next to (not instead of) the context
panel. It stays open while you move between areas, so you can keep asking while you work.

## Other surfaces

- The **notification panel** slides in from the right when you click the bell.
- The **Activity** drawer slides in from the right when you choose "View activity" on a row of
  the Users list.

## Page not found

If you open a wrong link you see "This page does not exist" with the buttons "Go back" and
"Back to home".

## Not available

There is no command palette and no global search across the application; search is
available inside individual lists (customers, users, chat conversations).

documents.title: Customers and contacts
documents.body:
# Customers and contacts

Open **Workspace → "Customers"**. The page is titled "Customers" — "The companies and people
you do business with."

## Company or individual

Each customer has a "Type":

- "Company" — an organization;
- "Individual" — a private person.

The type only describes the customer; both types have the same fields.

## The customer list

- **Search** — the box "Name, number, email or tax ID…" finds customers by name, legal name,
  email or tax ID, and by number: "C-000123", "000123" and "123" all find customer number 123.
- **Filters** — "Status" ("All statuses", "Active", "Inactive", "Archived") and "Type" ("All
  types", "Company", "Individual"). "Reset" clears them.
- **Columns** — "No.", "Customer", "Phone", "Status", "Owner", "Tags" (hidden by default),
  "Created". Click a sortable header ("No.", "Customer", "Status", "Created") to sort. The gear
  in the header row opens "Field settings", where you can show, hide and reorder columns, and
  "Reset to default".
- **Paging** — 20 rows per page by default; the footer shows "Total", the page and "Items per
  page".
- **Archived customers are hidden** from the list by default. Choose the "Archived" status
  filter to see them.

Inactive and archived rows are shown dimmed.

## Adding a customer

Click **"Add customer"**. Only "Name" is required — "everything else can be filled in later".
The dialog also has "Type" (defaults to "Company"), "Owner" (defaults to you), "Email" and
"Phone". Click "Create customer".

- A phone number is stored in international format — pick the country code and type the
  number; if you enter one, it must be a real, valid number.
- The customer's currency is taken from the organization's default currency.
- Names, emails and tax IDs do not have to be unique — two customers may share them.

## The customer page

Click a customer's name to open its page. The header shows the name, number and status badge,
with the buttons "Edit", "Archive" (or "Restore") and "Delete".

Tab **"Overview"**:

- "Upcoming" — calendar events linked to this customer, with "Schedule a meeting";
- "State" — "Status", "Owner", "Contacts", "Customer since";
- "Contact" — "Email", "Phone", "Website", "Address";
- "Business" — "Type", "Legal name", "Tax ID", "Currency", "External ID";
- "Tags", "Notes", and "Record" ("Created", "Last updated", "Customer ID").

Tab **"Contacts"** lists the customer's contact persons. The right side of the page shows the
customer's "Activity".

## Editing a customer

Click **"Edit"**. The "Edit customer" dialog has "Name", "Legal name", "Type", "Owner",
"Email", "Phone", "Website", the address ("Address line 1", "Address line 2", "City",
"Region", "Postal code", "Country (ISO code)" — a two-letter code such as `DE`), "Tax ID",
"Currency" (a three-letter code such as `EUR`) and "Notes". Click "Save changes".

Tags, language and external ID are shown on the page but cannot be edited in the interface.

## Owner

The owner is the colleague responsible for the customer. It must be an active user. A new
owner gets an in-app notification (User settings → "Notifications" → "Customers assigned to
me" turns it off). A customer can also be
"Unassigned".

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| "Active" | A customer you currently work with (the default). |
| "Inactive" | Temporarily not active; stays in the list, dimmed. |
| "Archived" | Hidden from the default list; nothing is deleted. |

Change the status from the row menu of the list ("Mark inactive", "Mark active", "Archive",
"Restore") or with "Archive"/"Restore" on the customer page. Any status can change to any
other. There are no sales stages such as lead or prospect.

## Archive or delete

- **Archive** hides the customer from the default list — "Nothing is deleted — you can
  restore them at any time."
- **Delete** removes the customer **permanently**, together with its contacts. It cannot be
  undone. Calendar events that were linked to the customer are kept but lose the link.
  Prefer archiving if you only want a customer out of the way.

## Customer numbers

Every customer gets a human-readable number when it is created, for example `C-000001`. The
number is assigned automatically and can never be changed or reused. By default numbers have
the prefix `C-` and six digits. An administrator can change the format (prefix, number of
digits) in Settings → "Numbering"; the new format then applies to the numbers of all existing
customers as they are displayed.

## Contact persons

On the "Contacts" tab click **"Add contact"**. Fields: "Name" (required), "Position", "Email",
"Phone", the switch "Primary contact", and "Notes". Click "Save".

- Only one contact can be primary; marking another one primary moves the flag.
- Use the row menu ("Contact actions") for "Edit contact" or "Delete". Deleting a contact is
  permanent.

## Who can do what

Every signed-in user can view, add, edit, archive and delete customers and their contacts —
there is no per-role restriction on customers.

## Not available

No import or export of customers, no bulk actions, no merging of duplicates, no parent/child
company hierarchy, no sales pipeline, and no file attachments on customers.

documents.title: Calendar and events
documents.body:
# Calendar and events

Open **"Calendar"** in the left rail. It opens the week view.

## Views and moving around

- View tabs: "Day", "Week" (default), "Month", "Agenda".
- "Today" jumps to the current period; the arrows ("Previous period" / "Next period") move
  back and forward.
- "Agenda" lists everything that has not ended yet, starting now, grouped by day ("Today",
  "Tomorrow", …). If it is empty: "Nothing scheduled ahead".
- The small month picker in the sidebar jumps to any date.
- In the month view a busy day shows "+N more".

### Keyboard shortcuts

Press `?` in the calendar to see them ("Keyboard shortcuts"). They work when no input field is
focused:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `T` | "Go to today" |
| `D` / `W` / `M` / `A` | "Day view" / "Week view" / "Month view" / "Agenda view" |
| `←` / `→` | "Previous period" / "Next period" |
| `N` or `C` | "New event" |
| `?` | "Show this help" |
| `Esc` | "Close panel or dialog" |

## Creating an event

Click **"New event"**, or click an empty slot in the grid to create an event at that time. The
event opens in the context panel on the right ("New event" — "Guests get an in-app invitation
right away."). Fields:

- "Title" (required);
- "All day" — when on, you pick "Date" and "Last day"; when off, "Date", "From" and "To". The
  end must be after the start;
- "Type" — "Meeting" (default), "Call", "Deadline", "Out of office", "Other". The type only
  changes the colour and icon;
- "Customer" — optionally link the event to a customer; it then appears in that customer's
  "Upcoming" card;
- "Guests" — colleagues to invite ("Add a guest");
- "Reminders";
- "Location", "Notes";
- "Private" — see "Who can see an event" below;
- "Show me as busy" (on by default).

Click **"Create"**. If the event overlaps another one you see "Overlaps with another event" —
this is only a warning.

An event ends at its end time exactly: a 10:00–11:00 meeting and an 11:00–12:00 meeting do not
overlap.

## Changing an event

Open the event and edit the fields, then click **"Save"**. In the grid you can also drag an
event to move it or drag its edge to change the duration; a message "Moved to …" or "Duration
changed" offers "Undo".

Right-click an event for "Open event", "Are you going?", "Duplicate", "Cancel event" /
"Restore" and "Delete".

**Only the organizer can change an event** — its time, fields, guests, status. Guests see the
fields disabled. If you try anyway, the error is "Only the organizer can modify this event".

## Cancel or delete

- **"Cancel event"** keeps the event, marked as cancelled, and notifies the guests. It can be
  undone with "Restore". A cancelled event stays visible in the day, week and month views,
  marked as cancelled; the "Agenda" view and the "Upcoming" lists leave it out.
- **"Delete"** removes the event for everyone, permanently — "Cancel the event instead if you
  want to keep the history."

## Guests and answers (RSVP)

The organizer is always a guest of their own event and is marked as going. Invited colleagues
get an in-app invitation. As a guest you answer under **"Are you going?"** with "Yes", "Maybe"
or "No", and can "Add a note (optional)". Change your answer at any time. The organizer is
notified of your answer.

Each guest shows a badge: "Going", "Maybe", "Declined" or "No reply".

Only active users of your organization can be guests; customers and their contacts cannot be
invited, and there are no email invitations.

## Reminders

Reminders are **personal**: each person sets their own on an event, up to 5. Choose from "At
the start", 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes, 1 or 2 hours, 1 day or 1 week before ("Add a reminder",
"Remove reminder").

- A reminder arrives as an **in-app notification** — "… starts soon". There are no email or
  phone reminders.
- If you do not choose, the organization default is used: 10 minutes before a timed event, and
  09:00 on the previous day for an all-day event (administrators can change the defaults).
- When the event is moved, reminders move with it; when it is cancelled or deleted, they are
  removed.
- A reminder that could not be delivered within about 10 minutes of its time is skipped.

You can turn off "Event reminders" in User settings → "Notifications".

## Who can see an event

You see an event if you are its organizer, its creator or one of its guests. In addition,
everyone in the organization can see an event **linked to a customer** — unless the event is
marked **"Private"**. "Private" removes exactly that organization-wide visibility; guests still
see it.

Administrators do not see other people's events, with one exception: events whose organizer's
account was deleted can be seen and managed by administrators.

## Time zones

Every event is stored with its time zone. Your calendar is drawn in **your** time zone
(User settings → "Profile" → "Time zone"), or the organization's default zone if you left it
empty. If your device is in a different zone, the sidebar warns "Times are shown in …".

## Not available

No recurring (repeating) events, no email invitations or reminders, no shared team or
resource calendars, no booking pages, and no synchronisation with external calendars.

documents.title: Users and roles
documents.body:
# Users and roles

User accounts are managed on **Workspace → "Users"** — "Manage the people who can sign in to
this organization."

## Roles

| Role | Shown as | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `USER` | "User" | The regular role. |
| `ADMIN` | "Admin" | Manages user accounts (add, change password, change avatar, disable/enable, delete). Opens the "Settings" area and can change organization settings (name, currency, calendar defaults, numbering). Can also see and manage calendar events whose organizer's account was deleted. |

There are only these two roles; there are no custom roles or fine-grained permissions.
Administrators do **not** get access to other people's private data: they cannot read someone
else's calendar events, chat conversations, notifications or assistant conversations.

Everyone in the organization can open the Users page and see the list and each person's page.
Only administrators see and can use the actions that change accounts: "Add user", changing a
password or avatar, disabling or enabling access, and deleting. A regular user sees the list
without these actions and cannot flip the "Active" switch.

## The user list

- Search "Search by email or name…", filter "Status" ("All statuses", "Active", "Inactive").
- Columns: "User", "Phone", "Role", "Active", "Last seen" ("Online", "Never signed in" or "Last
  seen …"), "Created".
- The "Active" column is a switch: an administrator can flip it to enable or disable access
  directly in the list.
- Row checkboxes select users; the "Export selected" button that appears is a placeholder and
  is always disabled — bulk actions and export are not available.

## Adding a user

There is no self-registration and no email invitation. To give someone access, click
**"Add user"** and fill in:

- "Email" (required, unique in the organization — a duplicate shows "Already exists");
- "Name" (optional);
- "Role" ("User" or "Admin", default "User");
- "Phone" (optional);
- "Initial password" (required, 12 to 128 characters).

Click "Create user", then give the person their email and initial password in a safe way.
They receive a welcome email, are added automatically to the organization's default chat
channel, and administrators get the notification about a new user. Ask the new user to
change the password in User settings → "Security".

## Changing someone's password

Row menu → **"Change password"** (or the button on the user's page). Enter "New password" and
"Confirm password" (12–128 characters). No current password is needed. "The user will be
signed out of all sessions and will need the new password to sign in again." The user gets a
notification that their password was changed.

People who forgot their own password can reset it themselves with "Forgot password?" on the
sign-in page.

## Disabling and enabling access

Row menu → **"Disable access"**: the user "will not be able to sign in, and all their sessions
will be signed out." Their data stays. "Enable access" gives access back. You cannot disable
yourself ("You cannot disable yourself").

Prefer disabling over deleting for people who leave.

## Deleting a user

Row menu → **"Delete"**: "This will permanently delete … This action cannot be undone." Their
customers become "Unassigned", and calendar events they organized lose their organizer (an
administrator can still manage those events). You cannot delete yourself.

## Avatar

Row menu → **"Change avatar"** uploads a profile picture for the user (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF).

## The user page

Click a user to open their page: badges for role and "Active"/"Inactive" (and "You" on your
own record), the cards "State", "Contact", "Account", "Avatar", "Record" and "Activity", and
the buttons "Change password", "Change avatar", "Disable access"/"Enable access", "Delete".

There is no form to edit another user's name, phone or role in the interface; people edit
their own name and phone in User settings → "Profile". To change someone's role, currently
the only way in the interface is to create the account with the right role.

## Activity

Row menu → **"View activity"** opens the "Activity" drawer: account creation, password changes,
signing out of all devices, enabling/disabling and email changes are recorded there.

documents.title: Account security, passwords and devices
documents.body:
# Account security, passwords and devices

Everything here is in **User settings** (account menu at the bottom of the sidebar → "User
settings").

## Changing your password

User settings → **"Security"** → "Password" — "Changing your password signs you out
everywhere else." Fill in "Current password", "New password" and "Confirm new password", then
click "Change password".

- The new password must be 12 to 128 characters long. There are no other rules — a long
  passphrase is a good choice.
- A wrong current password shows "Current password is incorrect".
- All your other browsers and devices are signed out; the device you are using stays signed
  in.
- You can change your password at most 10 times per hour.

## Forgot your password

1. On the sign-in page click **"Forgot password?"**.
2. Enter your "Email" (and "Organization (optional)" if you normally fill it in) and click
   "Send reset link". You always see "If that email exists, a reset link is on its way. It
   expires in 60 minutes." — the page does not reveal whether an account exists.
3. Open the link from the email, choose "New password" and "Confirm new password", and click
   "Reset password". You are signed in, and all other sessions are signed out.

If the link is too old or already used you see "This link is invalid or has expired." — use
"Request a new reset link". You can request at most 3 reset links per hour.

## Changing your email address

User settings → **"Account"** → "Change email" — "We'll send a confirmation link to the new
address before it takes effect." Enter "New email" and your "Current password", then click
"Send confirmation link". Open the link sent to the new address within 60 minutes to confirm;
your old address then receives a notice about the change. Until you confirm, the old address
stays in effect.

## Signed-in devices (sessions)

User settings → **"Security"** → "Active sessions" — "Devices that are currently signed in to
your account." Each row shows the device, its IP address and when it was last used; your
current device is marked "This device".

- **"Sign out"** on a row signs that device out; it will have to sign in again. Signing out
  your own device takes you back to the sign-in page.
- **"Sign out everywhere else"** signs out all other browsers and devices; this device stays
  signed in.
- "Ending a session closes its live connection immediately; ongoing requests from that device
  stop working within 15 minutes."

If you see a device you do not recognise, sign it out and change your password.

## How long you stay signed in

You stay signed in while you use the application. A session ends after 7 days without any use,
and in any case 30 days after you signed in; then you sign in again.

## Security notifications

You always receive (and cannot turn off) in-app notifications for: password changes
("Password changes"), a sign-in from a new device ("Sign-ins from new devices" — "New sign-in
from … "), and "Suspicious session activity" — a sign that someone may have copied your
session; if you get it, change your password.

## Sign-in problems

- **"Invalid email or password"** — the email or the password is wrong. Check the keyboard
  layout and Caps Lock, or use "Forgot password?".
- **"Account is deactivated"** — your access or your whole organization has been disabled.
  Contact your administrator.
- **Too many attempts** — after 5 sign-in attempts with the same email within a minute you
  must wait a minute before trying again ("Too many attempts"). There is no permanent lock-out.
- If you are suddenly taken back to the sign-in page, your session ended (signed out on
  another device, password changed, or expired). Sign in again.

## Not available

No two-factor authentication, no passkeys, no single sign-on (Google, Microsoft, SAML), and
no "remember me" choice.

documents.title: Notifications
documents.body:
# Notifications

Notifications are in-app only: they appear in the application, never by email or phone.

## The bell

The bell in the header opens the notification panel. The badge on the bell counts
notifications that arrived **since you last opened the panel** (up to "99+"); opening the
panel clears the badge. A notification stays **unread** until you open it or mark it read.

New notifications also pop up briefly in the corner of the screen while the panel is closed
("Dismiss" hides the pop-up).

## The panel

- Tabs: "Unread", "All" (default) and "Archived".
- Click a notification to mark it read and go to the user, customer, event or chat conversation it is about.
- The row menu ("Notification actions") offers "Mark as read" / "Mark as unread" and "Archive"
  / "Restore". Archiving removes a notification from "All" without deleting it.
- "Mark all as read" at the bottom marks everything read; "Load more" shows older ones.
- The gear ("Notification settings") opens the same switches as User settings →
  "Notifications".
- Empty tabs say "You're all caught up", "No notifications yet" or "Nothing archived".

## What you are notified about

You are never notified about your own actions.

| Setting name | When you get it | Can be turned off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "New users in the organization" | Someone created a user account (administrators only) | yes |
| "Welcome message" | Your account was created | yes |
| "Customers assigned to me" | You became the owner of a customer | yes |
| "Invitations to events" | You were invited to an event, or a cancelled event was restored | yes |
| "Event time changes" | An event you are invited to was moved | yes |
| "Replies to my events" | A guest answered an event you organize | yes |
| "Event reminders" | A reminder you set is due ("… starts soon") | yes |
| "New chat messages" | A colleague wrote in a conversation you are in while you were **not** looking at it | yes |
| "Password changes" | Your password was changed | no — "Always on" |
| "Event cancellations" | An event you are invited to was cancelled | no — "Always on" |
| "Sign-ins from new devices" | Someone signed in to your account from a new device | no — "Always on" |
| "Suspicious session activity" | Your session may have been copied | no — "Always on" |

Repeated notifications of the same kind (for example several changes to one event, or several
messages in one conversation) are combined into one entry while it is unread — a chat entry then
reads "N new messages". You do not get a chat notification for a conversation you have open at that
moment. Opening a conversation and reading it marks its chat notification read, on every device
where you are signed in. The switches are grouped by category; chat messages are under "Chat".

## Choosing what you receive

User settings → **"Notifications"** — "Choose what lands in your notification inbox." Flip the
switch next to a type. Security-related types show "Always on" and cannot be turned off.

## Not available

No email or push notifications, no snoozing, no digest, and no per-customer or per-event
subscriptions.

documents.title: Files and avatars
documents.body:
# Files and avatars

## Where you can upload files

Today the only upload in the interface is a **profile picture (avatar)**:

- your own: User settings → "Profile" → "Avatar" → "Change" (and "Remove");
- someone else's: Workspace → "Users" → row menu or user page → "Change avatar".

Drop an image on the drop zone ("Drop a file here or choose one") or click "Choose file".

## Allowed images

JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF. Keep the image under 10 MB, as the Profile page says. A small preview
is generated automatically.

## Upload errors

- "This file type is not allowed" — the file is not one of the image types above.
- "File is too large (max … MB)" — choose a smaller image.
- The file's content is checked after upload: a file whose content does not match its type
  (for example a renamed PDF with a `.png` extension) is rejected.
- "Could not set the avatar, please try again" — the upload did not finish; try again.

## How files are protected

Files are not public. Each time a file is shown, the application creates a short-lived private
link that stops working after a few minutes, so copying an image address and sharing it does
not give lasting access. Uploads that were started but never finished are cleaned up
automatically after a day.

## Not available

You cannot attach documents (PDF, Word, Excel or others) to customers, events or chat
messages, and there is no file library or shared drive. Chat has no attachments yet.

documents.title: Organization settings
documents.body:
# Organization settings

The **"Settings"** area in the left rail holds settings that apply to the whole organization.
It is visible to administrators only; everyone else is sent back to the Workspace. Everyone
can still _see the effects_ (for example the organization name and default time zone).

Settings for yourself only (profile, password, notifications, theme) are in **User settings**,
not here. A simple test: if the person left the company, would the setting leave with them?
Then it is a user setting.

## General

Settings → **"General"** — "Name, language and currency used across the organization."

- "Organization name" (up to 120 characters) — shown at the top of the sidebar.
- "Default language" — only "English" is available.
- "Default currency" — "ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD or EUR. New customers inherit it." Changing
  it does not change existing customers.
- "Sign-in identifier: … — changed by the platform operator only." This is the value people
  type into "Organization (optional)" on the sign-in page; you cannot change it here.

Click "Save changes" ("Settings saved").

## Calendar

Settings → **"Calendar"** — "Defaults for everyone in the organization. People can override
their own time zone in user settings."

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| "Default time zone" (an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin`) | `UTC` |
| "Week starts on" ("Sunday", "Monday", "Saturday") | Monday |
| "Work day starts" / "Work day ends" | 09:00 / 18:00 |
| "Default event length (minutes)" (5–1440) | 30 |
| "Default reminder (minutes before)" — "Set 0 to remind at the start." | 10 |
| "Default all-day reminder (minutes before)" — "900 means 09:00 on the previous day" | 900 |

Click "Save calendar settings". The default reminders apply to events created afterwards when
the creator does not pick reminders; existing reminders are not changed.

## Numbering

Settings → **"Numbering"** — "How human-readable numbers are issued for your records." There is
one series, "Customers", showing "Next number: …".

- "Prefix" (up to 16 characters, e.g. `C-`), "Minimum digits" (0–12 — "6 turns 123 into
  000123"), "Starting number" (used only before the first customer is created). Click "Save
  format". The format is applied to all customer numbers when they are displayed, including
  existing ones.
- "Next number" — "Can only move forward — earlier numbers are already issued. Use it after
  importing records from another system." Click "Move counter". A lower value is ignored.

Numbers never restart and are never reused, even after a customer is deleted.

## AI assistant

Settings → **"AI assistant"** — "The persona and instructions the AI assistant follows for
everyone in the organization."

- "Persona" — "Who the assistant is and how it sounds. Up to 500 characters."
- "Instructions" — "What to emphasize, tone and level of detail. Up to 4000 characters."

Both are optional; leave them empty to use the assistant as it is. Click "Save AI assistant
settings" ("AI assistant settings saved"). The change applies to the next question anyone asks.

"Sent to the AI provider" — the persona and instructions are sent to the external AI provider
together with every question, so do not put passwords, keys or personal data there.

"The assistant's built-in limits always apply and cannot be changed here": it has no access to
your data, cannot perform actions, does not guess beyond the documentation, and answers in the
language of the question. Instructions that ask for anything else are ignored.

Only administrators can open this page or read what is saved on it.

## Messaging

Settings → **"Messaging"** — "Provider account and channels that customer conversations arrive on."
Administrators connect a WhatsApp Business account here.

- Click "Connect WhatsApp" and enter the "WhatsApp Business Account ID" and an "Access token" from
  Meta Business (a system-user token that does not expire is recommended; a temporary token shows a
  countdown and stops working when it runs out). "App ID (optional)" and "App secret (optional)" must be
  given together; with them the token is checked and its kind, expiry and permissions are shown, without
  them the card says "Not verified". The token is stored encrypted and is never shown again — only its
  last four characters.
- If Meta rejects the token, the reason is shown under the field (for example a missing permission or an
  account the token cannot read) and nothing is saved.
- The account card shows "Access token", the numbers synced from Meta with their quality, a switch
  "Enabled" for each number and "Make default" (one default number per account). "Refresh" re-reads the
  numbers, "Update token" replaces the token, "Disconnect" removes it and stops sending.
- Under each number, "Webhooks" shows where WhatsApp currently delivers that number's events: "Delivered to this
  system", "Not delivered anywhere" or "Delivered to …" another host. "Subscribe" sends them here (a server
  address must be configured, otherwise "No public address is configured on the server."); for events that
  go to another host "Take over" asks you to confirm, because that service stops receiving the number's
  webhooks until you press "Unsubscribe". Nothing is subscribed automatically.
- "Show received webhooks" lists what WhatsApp has sent, with "Signature valid", "Signature invalid" or
  "Not checked", and "Show body" for the raw text. Every webhook is kept exactly as received; for a subscribed
  number, messages and delivery receipts in them also update the conversations. A request without a valid
  signature is refused.
- "Show recent provider calls" lists the latest calls to Meta (without message text or tokens).
- A number that is not subscribed does not get delivery and read receipts: "Delivery and read receipts arrive
  only for numbers subscribed to this system (see “Webhooks” on each number); otherwise a sent message stays at
  “sent”."

## Activity

Settings → **"Activity"** — "Who changed the organization settings, and when." A read-only list
of changes to General, Calendar, Numbering and AI assistant (it shows that the AI assistant
settings changed, not the text).

## Not available

No branding (logo, colours), no email/SMTP settings, no per-organization feature switches, no
custom roles or permissions, no billing or subscription settings. For the AI assistant you can set
only the persona and instructions — it cannot be switched off per organization, and there is no
usage report.

documents.title: User settings
documents.body:
# User settings

Your personal settings. Open them from the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar (your
avatar and name) → **"User settings"**. The sections are "Profile", "Account", "Security",
"Notifications" and "Appearance". Every user has them, whatever the role.

## Profile

"This is how you appear to other people in this organization."

- "Avatar" — "Change" or "Remove" your picture (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, under 10 MB).
- "Name" — "Your full name".
- "Phone".
- "Language" — only "English"; "Language of the emails we send you."
- "Time zone" — an IANA name such as `Europe/Kyiv`. "Leave empty to follow the organization
  default. Your calendar is drawn in this zone."

Click "Save changes" ("Profile updated").

## Account

"Facts about your account, and how to change your email."

- Your "Email" (read-only here), "Role" (`ADMIN` or `USER`), "Status", "Member since" and
  "Last seen".
- "Change email" — see "Account security, passwords and devices".

You cannot change your own role or status; ask someone who manages accounts.

## Security

"Password" (change your password) and "Active sessions" (see and sign out your devices). See
"Account security, passwords and devices".

## Notifications

"Choose what lands in your notification inbox." One switch per notification type; types
marked "Always on" cannot be turned off. See "Notifications".

## Appearance

"How this app looks on this device. The choice is stored in this browser only."

- "Theme" — "Light", "Dark" or "System" (follows your operating system). The same choice is
  available from the theme switcher in the header.
- "Color theme" — "Dark grey" or "Slate"; "Applies to both light and dark mode."

Because the appearance is stored in the browser, another browser or device keeps its own
choice.

## Not available

No interface language other than English, no date or number format choice, and no email
notification preferences (notifications are in-app only).

documents.title: Troubleshooting and error messages
documents.body:
# Troubleshooting and error messages

## Error codes

Every error from the server has a code. The application shows the message below for it —
either as a pop-up (for connection, access, rate-limit and server errors) or next to the form
you submitted.

| Code | Message shown | What it usually means and what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | "Validation failed" | Some fields are invalid; the form marks them. Fix the marked fields and submit again. |
| `BAD_REQUEST` | "Invalid request" | The request was understood but not accepted — for example a wrong current password, an end time before the start, an unknown owner. The form usually shows the exact reason. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | "Authentication required" | You are not signed in, or your session ended. Sign in again. On the sign-in page the reason is shown instead ("Invalid email or password", "Account is deactivated"). |
| `FORBIDDEN` | "Access denied" | Your role does not allow this action (for example changing organization settings without the Admin role, or changing an event you do not organize). Ask an administrator or the event organizer. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | "Not found" | The item does not exist, was deleted, or you are not allowed to see it (for example someone else's private event or a chat you are not part of). |
| `CONFLICT` | "Conflict" | The change clashes with existing data — for example the email is already used by another account ("Already exists"), or the assistant is still answering your previous question. |
| `CHANNEL_WINDOW_CLOSED` | "The 24-hour reply window is closed" | You tried to reply to a customer more than 24 hours after their last message. The messaging channel only allows free-text replies within 24 hours. Add an internal note instead, or wait for the customer to write again. |
| `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` | "Wait a minute and try again." | You did the same action too many times in a short period. Wait and try again. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | "Internal server error" | An unexpected problem on the server. Try again; if it repeats, tell your administrator what you did and when. |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | "Service temporarily unavailable, please try again" | The server or one of its services is temporarily unreachable. Try again in a moment. |

Pop-up titles: "Connection problem", "Access denied", "Too many attempts", "Service
unavailable", "Server error".

## Common field messages

- "Already exists" — the value must be unique (for example a user's email).
- "Invalid value", "Invalid format" — the value has the wrong form (an email without `@`, a
  phone number that is not valid, a website that is not a URL).
- "Value is too large" / "Value is too small" — too long or too short, or a number outside the
  allowed range (for example a password shorter than 12 characters).
- "Current password is incorrect" — the current password you typed is wrong.
- "Must be after the start" — an event's end is not after its start.
- "Unknown user" — the chosen owner or guest is not an active user.
- "You cannot disable yourself" — you tried to switch off your own access.

## Other messages

- "Cannot reach the server. Check your connection and try again." — your device is offline or
  the server cannot be reached.
- "Something went wrong. Please try again." — an unexpected response; try again.
- "This page does not exist" — the address is wrong or the item moved. Use "Back to home".
- "Could not load …" (the calendar, conversations, notifications, activity, your account) —
  reload the page; if it persists, the server may be unavailable.

## Common situations

- **I was sent back to the sign-in page.** Your session ended — signed out from another
  device, password changed by you or an administrator, 7 days without use, or 30 days since
  sign-in. Sign in again.
- **I cannot see the "Settings" area.** It is for administrators only.
- **I cannot change an event.** Only its organizer can.
- **A colleague's event is missing from my calendar.** You see only events you organize, were
  invited to, or that are linked to a customer and not private.
- **A customer disappeared from the list.** It may be archived — choose the "Archived" status
  filter. Deleted customers cannot be recovered.
- **New chat messages do not appear.** Chat updates on its own while the connection to the
  server is up. If a message is missing, the connection may have dropped: switch back to the
  window or reload the page, and the conversation catches up.
- **A conversation stays unread although I opened it.** A conversation counts as read only while
  the window is in front of you and the latest message is on screen. If you are scrolled up in the
  history or the window is in the background, the unread badge stays until you scroll to the
  newest message or come back to the window.
- **I see "… is typing…" above the message box.** A colleague who has the same conversation open
  is writing a message. It disappears when they send it or stop typing.
- **I did not get an email notification.** Notifications are in-app only; check the bell.
- **Times look shifted.** Your calendar uses the time zone from User settings → "Profile" (or
  the organization default); set it to where you are.
- **The assistant button is missing.** The assistant is not enabled in your installation.

## Assistant errors

- "The assistant is unavailable right now. Try again in a moment."
- "The assistant took too long to answer. Try again."
- "Something went wrong while answering. Try again."

Ask again after a moment. While an answer is being written you cannot send another question —
wait or click "Stop".

documents.title: Glossary
documents.body:
# Glossary

- **Organization** — your company's space in the application. All customers, events, chats
  and users belong to one organization and are invisible to other organizations.
- **Sign-in identifier** — the short name of your organization typed into "Organization
  (optional)" on the sign-in page.
- **User** — a person who can sign in to your organization. Also the name of the regular role.
- **Admin** — the role that can open the "Settings" area and change organization settings.
- **Area** — one section of the application, chosen in the icon rail on the left: "Workspace",
  "Calendar", "Chat", "Settings", "Playground", "Guide".
- **Icon rail** — the narrow column of area icons at the far left.
- **Sidebar** — the second column, with the navigation of the active area.
- **Context panel** — the column on the right that shows the details of one item (today, a
  calendar event) next to the page.
- **Assistant panel** — the right-most column with this AI assistant.
- **Dashboard** — the start page of the Workspace.
- **Customer** — a company ("Company") or a private person ("Individual") you do business
  with.
- **Contact (contact person)** — a person you talk to at a customer. One can be the "Primary
  contact".
- **Owner** — the colleague responsible for a customer.
- **Customer number** — the human-readable number of a customer, such as `C-000001`; assigned
  automatically, never changed or reused.
- **Status** — for customers: "Active", "Inactive" or "Archived".
- **Archive** — hide a customer from the default list without deleting it.
- **Event** — an entry in the calendar: a meeting, call, deadline, time out of office, or
  other.
- **Organizer** — the person who created an event and the only one who can change it.
- **Guest** — a colleague invited to an event.
- **RSVP** — a guest's answer to an invitation: "Yes" ("Going"), "Maybe" or "No" ("Declined").
- **Reminder** — a personal in-app notification before an event starts.
- **Private event** — an event linked to a customer that is not shown to the whole
  organization.
- **All-day event** — an event that covers whole days rather than a time range.
- **Time zone** — the zone your calendar is drawn in; yours in "Profile", or the
  organization's default.
- **Notification** — an in-app message in the bell panel; can be read, unread or archived.
- **Session** — one signed-in browser or device; listed under "Active sessions".
- **Conversation** — a chat between colleagues. The organization's default channel includes
  everyone.
- **Activity** — the history of important changes to a customer, user, event or the settings.
- **Numbering** — the settings that define how customer numbers look.
- **Assistant** — this AI help: it answers questions about how to use the product and has no
  access to your data.

documents.title: What the assistant can and cannot do
documents.body:
# What the assistant can and cannot do

This document describes the assistant itself — the panel you are talking to. The assistant
must follow it.

## What it is for

The assistant answers questions about **how to use this application**: where a feature lives,
what a field or status means, how a workflow goes, what an error message means. It answers
from the product documentation it was given. The panel always says: "AI assistant — answers
can be wrong. It has no access to your data."

## What it cannot do

- **It cannot see your data.** It has no access to your customers, contacts, events, users,
  chats, notifications, files or settings, and it does not know your name, email or
  organization. It knows only your role (User or Admin) and your language setting. Asked
  "how many customers do I have" or "when is my next meeting", it says it cannot see that and
  points to the screen where you can look it up (for example the "Customers" list or the
  calendar "Agenda").
- **It cannot act.** It cannot create, change or delete anything and cannot click anything for
  you. It explains the steps; you perform them.
- **It does not invent.** If the documentation does not cover a question, it says so instead of
  guessing, and suggests asking an administrator. It does not describe features that do not
  exist; when something is not available, it says so plainly.
- **It explains only what your role can do.** For actions reserved to administrators it says
  that an administrator is needed, instead of giving step-by-step instructions.

## How it answers

Your administrator can give the assistant a persona and extra instructions in Settings → "AI
assistant" (for example a name, a tone, or what to emphasize). Those instructions never change
the limits above: the assistant still cannot see your data, cannot act, does not guess, and
answers in the language of the question.

- In the language of the question.
- Short and concrete, using the exact names of buttons and menus as they appear on screen,
  and Markdown lists for steps.

## Using the panel

- Open or close it with the assistant button in the header ("Toggle assistant"); it stays open
  while you move around the application.
- Type a question in "Ask a question…" (up to 4000 characters) and press Enter or "Send";
  Shift+Enter adds a new line. While an answer is being written the button becomes "Stop".
- You can ask one question at a time; up to 10 questions per minute.
- **"New conversation"** starts over: the assistant forgets the previous questions. You have one
  conversation at a time; there is no list of past conversations.
- The assistant remembers the last 10 questions and answers of the current conversation.

## Privacy

Your questions are sent to an external AI provider to produce the answer. **Do not paste
passwords, keys or other secrets**, and avoid pasting personal data of customers or
colleagues. Administrators cannot read your conversation with the assistant.

documents.title: Chat
documents.body:
# Chat

Open **Chat** in the left rail. The list on the left has two tabs: "Customers" (conversations
that arrive from a messaging channel; this tab opens first) and "Team" (conversations with
colleagues). Each customer conversation row shows the linked customer's avatar and name (or the contact's
profile name when no customer is linked), the last message, and underneath a small label with the
channel it came through ("WhatsApp", or "Fake" for the built-in test channel), the person writing
and the channel's phone number. Customer conversations are drawn like a messenger chat: your
messages are green, the customer's are white (dark grey in the dark theme), over a patterned
background, with larger tick marks (grey = sent or delivered, blue = read).

## Team conversations

- Click "New conversation", pick colleagues under "Participants" and optionally give the
  conversation a "Name". The title is the other people's names when no name is set.
- Type in "Write a message…" and press Enter to send ("Send"); Shift+Enter starts a new line.
- A message that could not be delivered shows "Not sent" with "Retry" and "Discard".
- You see "… is typing…" while someone writes, and unread counts in the list.
- Only participants can open a team conversation — not even an administrator who is not in it.

## Customer conversations

Customer conversations appear under "Customers" when a customer writes to your messaging
channel. They are visible to every active user of the organization, and a conversation has a
status ("Open", "Pending", "Resolved") and an optional assignee.

- Reply with "Reply to customer"; use "Internal note" for a note only your team sees — a note is
  never sent to the customer and does not change the inbox order.
- A free-text reply is only possible within **24 hours** of the customer's last message. After that
  the composer explains that the window is closed and offers only "Internal note"; the customer
  writing again reopens the window.
- Each of your replies shows its delivery state next to the time: a clock (sending), one tick
  (sent), two ticks (delivered), two highlighted ticks (read). A failed reply shows the reason and
  "Resend" (not offered when the 24-hour window is closed).
- Replying to a conversation nobody is assigned to assigns it to you; replying to a "Resolved" one
  reopens it. The assignee gets a notification ("New customer messages") when the customer writes,
  unless they already have the conversation open.
- In a conversation's contact panel you can link the contact to a customer or create one.

Customer conversations need a connected messaging channel; an administrator connects WhatsApp under
Settings → "Messaging". Once a number is subscribed there ("Webhooks" → "Subscribe"), a customer's WhatsApp
message creates a conversation (or adds to the open one) under "Customers", and your replies show their
delivery state: one tick (sent), two ticks (delivered), two highlighted ticks (read). A reply WhatsApp could not
deliver shows the reason and "Resend". A customer's message that is not text (a photo, document, voice note…) appears as "Message not supported (image)" — it is not downloaded yet. A customer's reaction to a message appears as "Reacted 👍" (or "Removed a reaction") and does not reopen the 24-hour window. When you open a customer's message in a WhatsApp conversation, the customer sees it as read (blue ticks) on their phone. Without a subscription a sent
message stays at "sent" and the composer says "Delivery and read receipts are not tracked on this channel yet:
a message stays at “sent”."

To write to a customer first, open the "Customers" tab, click "New customer conversation", pick the
"WhatsApp number", enter the "Customer phone" in international format (for example +380501234567) and
click "Start". If that number already has an open conversation, it opens instead. Outside the 24-hour
window only an approved template can be sent: click "Send template", enter the "Template name" and
"Language code" (for example hello_world and en_US) and click "Send". Templates with variables are not
supported yet; if the template does not exist in that language, or the number is not allowed on a test
account, the message shows as failed with "Resend".

## Notifications

A colleague's message creates a "New chat messages" notification (category "Chat") only when you are
not looking at that conversation; several messages are combined into one entry, and opening the
conversation clears it. You can turn it off in User settings → "Notifications".
